title: Abelianisation of the MI integral on exceptional divisors
html:
Proposition. Abelianisation of the MI integral on exceptional divisors

Let \mathcal{S}_c \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) be the exceptional divisor at a branch point z_c (Bring's surface smoothness), and let (\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+) be the connection--curvature pair of the (mass identity). For each vertical degree n \geq 0 in the Reeb decomposition, the restriction of the nonabelian multiplicative integral to \mathcal{S}_c abelianises to the n-th prolonged Seiberg--Witten period:

\begin{equation}\label{eq:mi-sw-abelianisation}
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_{\mathcal{S}_c}
  \bigl(\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+\bigr)
  \bigr\rVert_{J^n}
  = 
  \bigl\lvert a_D^{(n)}\bigr\rvert
  = 
  \biggl\lvert\oint_{\mathcal{S}_c}\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}^{(n)}\biggr\rvert,
\end{equation}

where \lVert\cdot\rVert_{J^n} denotes the Killing-form norm projected onto the n-th jet component, and \lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}^{(n)} is the n-th prolonged Seiberg--Witten differential.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs—real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. The generic categorical/q-deformation identities it relies upon remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
